but I don't really know how to handle money at all

Okay, this is a real problem. And not one that can be solved in a Voat post. But some basic ideas:

  • Get a better job. Don't care if you like it. Look, I went from a software analyst to pizza delivery once. The economy where I lived was crap, everything was swirling down the toilet, and I got caught up in it. I hated delivering pizzas, but it paid. Lights stayed on, rent got paid.

  • Make a budget and be honest with yourself!

  • Start with the absolute necessities. Rent. Utilities. Food (again- honesty!). Find out what they cost and plug them in. You can't be financially independent if you don't know how much that costs. Then list the things you want and use. Finally, the stuff you're okay living without.

  • Cut what you can cut. Cell phones are just about mandatory these days. $1000 "flagship phones" with unlimited data for dozens of devices are not. Determine what you need and stick with it. Same with other expenses. Especially small monthly subscription fees. A couple of years ago, I got rid of almost all of my <25.00/month subscriptions that I didn't use or could live without. Saved hundreds of dollars a month.

  • Find out what you need to live reasonably, once you've made some tough decisions on what you need as opposed to what you want. Then, and this is the hard part, stick to it. Financial discipline is tough. Believe me. And it doesn't get easier when you make more money- you just have the ability to dig yourself even deeper. "Hey look- it's a $5000 TV. We can just charge it and pay it off!" This is where my wife steps in. I often say that without her, I'd lived in the best equipped refrigerator box in the city.

  • Stop letting your parents carry you. Tough decision, but you'll never be independent like this. Now, that doesn't mean take nothing from them. I have a friend who's a widowed mom going to school to get a better job. Her parents and her son's grandparents are fairly well off and make sure that she and her son are taken care of. As long as she's going to school. They're a support net, but they don't pay her way in life. In other words, they take care of her while she's getting what she needs to begin taking care of herself.

  • Get out of San Francisco. The cost of living there is beyond expensive. Beyond ridiculous.

I just wish there was a way to not scale back standard of living so much. Ever heard of golden handcuffs? That's kinda what it feels like.

You're probably right about moving out of the city if I give up their support. Do you think I could get better at this stuff while still letting them pay rent? I'd really hate to leave.

More importantly, managing your finances isn't all that different from managing a business' finances. You might be able to get some good advice just by telling someone there that the "business" you need financial help with is your personal finances. Will it work? Don't know.
